# A code patch refreshes only the patching core's I-cache

The firmware has no cross-core way to publish code changes; other cores can keep running stale cached lines.

**Category:** hazard · <span class="pill pill-planned">Single source</span>
{ .facts }

**Build:** [E-M10 Mark II firmware 1.4, build 1400](../firmware/em10-ii-1400.md) · **Cameras:** [Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II](../cameras/em10-ii.md)

After a write through the uncached alias, write the D-cache back and invalidate the I-cache of the core that patched. For an entry another core may run, keep the patched bytes in one aligned 8-byte line, patch while no other core can be inside it, and pass that core's calls through.

> **What happens:** A core with a stale line runs old code, or a half-written jump if the patched bytes span two lines.

**Symptoms:** [Restarts or crashes when a feature runs](index.md#restart-in-use)

## Observations

- **Static analysis** ([fenykl](../projects/fenykl.md)): No cross-core publication protocol found in the E-M10 Mark II 1.4 firmware; the hook rules follow from it. Source: [fenykl plugin SDK](../sources/fenykl.sdk.md).

**[Full detail upstream](https://github.com/atx/fenykl/blob/dd8dde0ead63bfc2a722f65a7b86e19577ad9778/sdk/README.md#hooks)**
